!3 CSV: what is equal and what is not
Two cells that both read as numbers compare by value (10 = 10.00); otherwise the text must be identical (no trim), so with a semicolon separator 1,5 is text. Quoted fields follow RFC 4180: the separator and line breaks inside quotes, "" for a quote. A wildcard is a whole cell: !-${any}-!, !-${any-string}-! and !-${ignore}-! accept any value, !-${any-number}-! a decimal number, !-${regex:P}-! the whole cell.

|script|csv comparison|
|separator|;|
|check|compare;|{{{id;amount
1;10}}}|{{{id;amount
1;10.00}}}|OK|
|check not|compare;|{{{id;price
1;1,5}}}|{{{id;price
1;1,50}}}|OK|
|check not|compare;|{{{id;v
1;a}}}|{{{id;v
1; a}}}|OK|
|check|compare;|{{{id;note;quote
1;"a;b
c";"say ""hi"""}}}|{{{id;note;quote
1;"a;b
c";"say ""hi"""}}}|OK|
|check|compare;|!-id;at;n;s;x
${any};${regex:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}};${any-number};${any-string};${ignore}-!|{{{id;at;n;s;x
7;14:05;-3.5;hello;}}}|OK|
|check not|compare;|!-id;n
1;${any-number}-!|{{{id;n
1;abc}}}|OK|
